agree.reason: The visit log and survey make a clear, personal case, but a board member who doubts the athletic and bus costs gets reassurance more than answers, so they may stay unconvinced.

honest.reason: The piece rightly stops short of promising a higher graduation rate, but it adds facts the brief doesn't support: the body-clock claim and the 11 p.m. figure, the claim that first period is the class students miss most, and the line that every student pays the cost every day.

works_the_facts.reason: Useful figures are worked out (412 against 369 combined, about three in four sleeping under seven hours, one in six not graduating on time), but the $180,000 is never put per student and the one-point attendance gain is never turned into school days.

right_comparison.reason: Today's 7:25 start is shown through real first-period data, and the comparison district is used fairly, but the piece never says what happens to the 84% if nothing changes.

qualification.reason: The promise to track tardies, attendance and course failures and report after year one is checkable, but it sets no target numbers and no consequence if they're missed beyond 'I'll say so.'

objections.reason: All three objections are raised fairly, but the bus answer is a vague trade-off, the athletics answer passes the work to the other district, and the plan to open the building at 7:15 brings its own staffing cost that the piece never mentions.

fit.reason: It is a well-formed op-ed with a headline and byline, but at roughly 700 words or more it runs past the 650-word limit.
